bull.b: Rapid revenue growth, record backlog and raised guidance provide durable visibility into demand. The backlog supports future sales conversion while continued expansion indicates strong adoption of the company’s solar infrastructure platforms.

High EBITDA and substantial free cash flow show that revenue growth is translating into meaningful earnings and internal funding. This supports investment, strategic expansion and shareholder returns without relying heavily on external financing.

bull.t: Low leverage and expanding product platform
bull.b: A net-cash balance sheet provides financial resilience, while faster growth in eBOS, foundations and other non-tracker products broadens the offering. Greater product breadth can improve attach rates, customer value and long-term market reach.

bear.t: Near-term margin pressure from investment and logistics
bear.b: The power-conversion investment should support future growth, but incremental costs and persistent logistics pressures may compress margins and operating leverage over the next several quarters. Returns will depend on successful scaling of the new platform.

Regulatory approval can delay or prevent the transaction, while integration may require additional capital and management attention. The acquired business is expected to contribute only small revenue initially, increasing execution risk before benefits become material.

Although TTM cash generation is strong, inconsistent conversion from earnings suggests working-capital or project-timing sensitivity. This can make investment capacity less predictable and indicates that reported profitability may not translate evenly into recurring cash.
